The '''1969–70 Football League Cup''' was the tenth season of the [[Football League Cup]], a knockout competition for England's top 92 football clubs. The competition started on 12 August 1969 and ended with the final on 7 March 1970.

The final was contested by [[1969–70 Football League First Division|First Division]] team [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] and [[1969–70 Football League First Division|First Division]] side [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] in London. [[Jeff Astle]] opened the scoring for Albion after five minutes, becoming the first player to score in the final of both the League Cup and FA Cup at Wembley. He had already scored in the first leg of the 1966 League Cup Final four years previously at West Ham United's Boleyn Ground. City equalised through [[Mike Doyle (footballer)|Mike Doyle]] to send the game into extra-time, and eventually won 2–1, with [[Glyn Pardoe]] scoring the winner.

This was the first season in which all ninety-two football league clubs competed in the tournament.

==Calendar==
Of the 92 teams, 36 received a [[Bye (sports)|bye]] to the second round (teams ranked 1st–35th in the [[1968–69 Football League]], plus 1969 League Cup winners [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]]) and the other 56 played in the first round. Semi-finals were [[Two-legged tie|two-legged]].
